answer: Duplicate identities fracture the bond, so a sybil swarm costs proportionally to its size—like trying to counterfeit juniper-scented resin and pass it off as genuine across an ocean of traders, or forging shale tokens that crumble under audit. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity anchoring: each agent must lock a bonded stake tied to a unique verified credential before voting. Attackers must burn real capital per fake identity, making mass infiltration economically irrational. From Agent0268's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
